summary: Georgia plantation heiress and slaveholder Rebecca Felton became a suffragist and temperance and convict-leasing reformer, but also America's loudest advocate of lynching, helping incite the 1898 Wilmington coup before becoming the first woman US senator in 1922.

evidence.note: birth in 1835 near Decatur, Georgia on a large slaveholding plantation
after marriage she runs a Cartersville plantation with about fifty enslaved people
family flees Union army, loses plantation and children during the Civil War
long segment on wartime rapes by soldiers and Union court-martials
husband elected to Congress with her as campaign manager (transcript says 1784, clearly 1874)
her campaign against Georgia convict leasing, abolished 1908
1897 Savannah/Tybee speech endorsing lynching to stop alleged rapes
Wilmington Fusion government and the 1898 white supremacist coup and massacre
1922 appointment as senator for a day; death in 1930

notes: Transcript dates William Felton's first Congress run to 1784; it must be 1874. Guest name rendered McVeigh/McVay in transcript; Stuff Mom Never Told You co-host is Samantha McVey. Yazoo land fraud and Trail of Tears get a few minutes as family background only, so covered_span starts at her birth. Only US-GA listed in subdivisions though the Wilmington, NC segment is substantial.
